newsitem.title: USA: GAO says U.S. Treasury debt actions proper.
newsitem.headline: GAO says U.S. Treasury debt actions proper.

text.p: A congressional watchdog agency concluded Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin acted within his authority while juggling funds to avoid a government spending default during the 1995-96 debt ceiling crisis.

The report by the General Accounting Office, issued by Treasury on Thursday, said Treasury "acted in accordance with statutory authority" throughout a series of actions to avoid exceeding the $4.9 trillion debt ceiling.
The debt ceiling was finally raised to $5.5 billion last March after protracted wrangling between the Republican-controlled Congress and the Clinton administration.

During the debt limit maneuvering, Rubin initiated several strategies to stay under the legally set ceiling including suspending some investments in some government trust funds and not reinvesting some of the Exchange Stabilization Fund's maturing Treasury securities.
Treasury also issued some securities to government trust funds without counting them toward the debt ceiling so that it could make Social Security payments.
The GAO said there were some losses of interest to government trust funds as a result of Treasury's actions but it cited no evidence that any of it exceeded legal authority.

Republican congressional leaders were seeking to tie approval of a debt-limit increase to acceptance of their budget-balancing proposals and tried to pressure the White House into doing so by using the debt cap as a pressure point.
House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer had warned Rubin's actions to avoid an interruption in borrowing and to avert a default risked bringing on a constitutional crisis.
Other Republicans spoke of potential impeachment proceedings against Rubin becasue they claimed his actions usurped Congress' constitutional control over spending.
